Inspiration is a game mechanic in Baldur's Gate 3. Inspiration points can be spent to re-roll certain failed d20 rolls, and are earned by making choices which fit the player character's background. Inspirations are shared between all party members.

Gaining Inspiration Points

Inspiration points are gained by completing specific actions in keeping with a character's background while that character is in the active party. These actions vary considerably; they can be anything from helping someone in need to finding certain loot, talking to certain characters or solving a problem using skills relevant to the character's background. If two characters have the same background, they can both gain an Inspiration point for the same action; occasionally some actions count for multiple backgrounds as well. Most backgrounds have pairs of mutually exclusive actions which both grant Inspiration points, making it impossible to achieve all of the goals for those backgrounds in a single playthrough.

The party cannot have more than 4 Inspiration points at any time. If an Inspiration trigger is hit while there are already 4 Inspiration points held by the party, the character still earns experience points (see below) but no Inspiration point is rewarded. The number of Inspiration points currently held by the party is tracked on the top right corner of the inventory sheet, between camp supplies and gold.

See each individual background's page for a list of actions which grant Inspiration points:

  •  Acolyte -  Shadowheart and  Zenith Feur'sel
  •  Charlatan -  Astarion and  Kree Derryck
  •  Criminal -  Ver'yll Wenkiir
  •  Entertainer -  Brinna Brightsong
  •  Folk Hero -  Wyll,  Minsc and  Danton
  •  Guild Artisan -  Jacelyn
  •  Haunted One -  The Dark Urge only
  •  Noble -  Minthara and  Kerz
  •  Outlander -  Karlach,  Halsin,  Eldra Luthrinn and  Sina'zith
  •  Sage -  Gale and  Sir Fuzzalump
  •  Soldier -  Lae'zel,  Jaheira and  Varanna Sunblossom
  •  Urchin -  Maddala Deadeye

A custom origin character may have any background except Haunted One.

Experience reward

Main article: Experience

When a party member earns an Inspiration they also gain a fixed amount of experience based on the action they completed. The experience rewards begin at 20 experience and increase in fixed increments up to 275, with the amount granted generally increasing for sources of inspiration found further into the game.

Inspiration is the only source of experience in the game not normally shared amongst all characters. Specifically, as a rule of thumb, only the character earning an Inspiration gets experience from doing so (which often leads to some party members having more experience than others). However, it is often possible for the player character in question to share experience earned from inspirations with others. To do so, the lead player character must be alone and the only member of the active party at the time the experience from the inspiration is granted (no companions). Afterwards, other companions gain this experience upon rejoining the party.

Spending Inspiration

Inspiration can be used with any roll made through the d20 roll menu. These rolls are predominately, but not exclusively, made during dialogue and are typically  Ability Checks, but occasionally may be  Saving Throws or even  Attack Rolls. Any d20 rolled in the background is not eligible to be re-rolled with Inspiration. Such rolls include attack rolls and saving throws made in normal combat, automatic skill checks made during exploration, and Sleight of Hand checks to pickpocket.

When a character fails an eligible roll and an Inspiration is available, the player is presented with the option to "Roll Again" by spending an Inspiration point. The number of currently available Inspiration points is shown in parentheses after the "Use Inspiration" text.

All modifiers for the original roll apply to the re-roll, including  Advantage or  Disadvantage and additional dice from  Guidance and similar effects such as  Lucky. A failed check can be re-rolled multiple times until the player character runs out of Inspiration or succeeds.

If the failed roll is a Sleight of Hand check to pick a lock or disarm a trap, the option to roll again using Inspiration is presented alongside the option to roll again using another Trap Disarm Toolkit or set of Thieves' Tools, if any are available. Note that attempting to use another Trap Disarm Toolkit results in the trap triggering on the player character, whereas using an inspiration does not trigger the trap.
